_note: Curation, as DATA. Everything here is the part of the kit that is a judgement
rather than a measurement: which pose serves which kind of shot, which plates a
chapter type may reach for, and the one line that tells a writer what a plate is
FOR. Geometry never appears here — that comes off the engine, which drew it.
It lives beside the manifests because a kit is swapped in as a whole. Ingest
reads whatever roles.json ships with the delivery and stamps it into the
registry; the pipeline then asks the registry for a role and never holds a list
of asset names. That is the test: a new kit with a different set of poses and a
different plate library drops in by shipping its own roles.json, and no Python
changes.
Which poses serve which kind of shot. `talks` is false where the pose has talk
frames on disk for continuity of the file set but using them looks like a
mistake (scripts/host.txt, TRAPS). `limit` caps how often a pose may appear in
one video — head-in-hands is the cost of being right, not a reaction to a mild
loss.
THE FRAMINGS ARE NOT POSES. close-up and medium are camera distances with no
floor line: they are the whole shot rather than a cut-out standing in a room,
so they are never solved onto a host-anchor. The close-up is the shot that was
missing — it carries the confession, the turn, and the line a chapter rests on.
A GLANCE IS CUT AGAINST THE SIDE THE GRAPHIC IS ON. Every glance key publishes
its eyeline as `glance` in the registry; a glance cut against a graphic on the
opposite side is worse than him facing camera, so straight-to-camera stays the
default and a glance is only chosen when the side is known.

host/leaning-on-desk.purpose: the default — talking to camera, weight on one arm

host/hands-in-pockets.purpose: listening, or between arguments. Neutral, low energy

host/holding-a-page.purpose: reading a figure out, when the page is the source of the number on screen

host/pointing-down-at-desk.purpose: the number is on the desk — pairs with a table or chart in the lower half

host/head-in-hands.purpose: the cost of being right. Weary, not comic — never for a mild loss

host/walking-out-of-frame.purpose: the exit. Last host frame of a section, never mid-argument

host/close-up.purpose: head and shoulders, down the lens — the confession, the turn, and the line a chapter rests on

host/medium.purpose: waist up, down the lens — a talking beat with more air than the close-up and no room behind him

host/close-up-glance-left.purpose: close-up looking off to camera-left; cut only against a graphic on THAT side

host/close-up-glance-right.purpose: close-up looking off to camera-right; cut only against a graphic on THAT side

host/medium-glance-left.purpose: medium looking off to camera-left; the two-shot's own eyeline

host/medium-glance-right.purpose: medium looking off to camera-right; the two-shot's own eyeline

host/medium-robe.purpose: the second wardrobe, at medium — a garment needs waist-up to show at all

_note: Which room angle opens a section, carries a talking beat, or backs a plate.
THREE CAMERA POSITIONS, NOT NINE STRAIGHT-ON ELEVATIONS. corner-perspective,
low-desk-height and high-desk-down exist because a cut made only of
eye-level frontal plates reads as props sliding on a shelf. They are in the
rotation, not a special case.
high-desk-down declares `hostAnchor: false` — looking down at the desk there
is no floor for him to stand on — so it is a SURFACE angle and never carries
a host. wall-of-calls refuses an anchor for the same reason.
panel is the TWO-SHOT: him on one side, the thing being discussed on
the other. The angles here are the ones with lateral room — a corner
or a wall — because a straight-on desk shot puts him in the middle of
the frame with nowhere for a graphic to go. `render_long` asked for
this role and nothing filled it, so every two-shot in the tag-driven
long was composed on flat ground with no room in it at all.
The sixteen generic types, fixed. The director returns one of these plus a
display title; the type decides which plates the chapter may use and the title
is the only thing that reaches the screen. A type may appear twice in one video
under different titles, so nothing here is a per-video identity — there are no
ordinals and no uniqueness.
`plates` is what this type adds to the universal set below. A plate named by
neither is not available to that chapter, and the validator says so by name.

_universal._why: titles, the set, the host, marks, row highlights and framed foreign media belong to every chapter

cold-open.purpose: the hook — the move, and why the next thirty minutes exist

how-we-got-here.purpose: the history that makes the present readable

how-the-money-is-made.purpose: the mechanism — what the business actually sells and to whom

the-numbers.purpose: the series, shown so it can be checked

one-framework.purpose: teach one idea the rest of the video leans on

moat.purpose: what stops someone else doing this

sector-comps.purpose: it did not move alone — the same moment across several names

management.purpose: who is running it, and what they have said

guidance-estimates.purpose: what they promised against what the street expects

short-interest.purpose: who is betting against it, and how crowded that is

valuation.purpose: what the price implies, and what it used to imply

filing-walk.purpose: the document itself, read on screen

bull-vs-bear.purpose: two readings that are both true

resigned-close.purpose: the sign-off — what he is left holding

purposes._note: One line per plate, for the writing prompt's catalogue. Taken from the kit's own scripts/*.txt so the catalogue and the artwork say the same thing.
purposes.tables/numbers-sheet-3r: three rows, six periods. The smallest sheet — use it rather than leaving rows empty
purposes.tables/numbers-sheet-6r: six rows, six periods. The full sheet
purposes.tables/numbers-sheet-6r-spark: six rows with a sparkline column; labels must be abbreviated, the spark takes real width
purposes.tables/numbers-sheet-4r-spark: four rows with a sparkline column; labels must be abbreviated
purposes.tables/cash-flow: the cash-flow statement — three groups, subtotals, a total
purposes.tables/multiples-strip: the subject against the peer set on several multiples at once — rows are METRICS, columns are subject / peer median / position on the peer range. Six rows in 16:9; the 9:16 re-author takes THREE rows and has no median column, so the peer number reaches the plate through marker-N's median argument instead. The inverse of peers/peer-strip, never a substitute for it
purposes.charts/line-6y: six periods, points labelled. The default series chart. Always after a table of the same series
purposes.charts/bars-6y: six periods as bars. When the periods are independent quantities rather than a path
purposes.charts/line-dense: many observations, four period heads, three marks. A price or daily series
purposes.figures/big-number-l1: one quantity: kicker, value, label, caption
purposes.figures/big-number-l2: one quantity plus a qualifier the number cannot carry alone
purposes.figures/big-fraction: a ratio, shown as what it is made of
purposes.figures/compare-side: two quantities side by side — two different things at the same time
purposes.figures/compare-stacked: two quantities stacked with a delta — the same measure at two times
purposes.cards/definition: kicker, term, body, example. The example is not optional
purposes.cards/quote-pull: management's own words, verbatim. If it needs an ellipsis it is too long
purposes.cards/criteria: a test being applied — three check/row pairs
purposes.structure/both-true: two statements that appear to conflict and are both true. mark-1/mark-2 take one up and one down
purposes.structure/unit-ladder: a top-line quantity walked down to an outcome in five steps
purposes.structure/row-spotlight: one row of a table pulled out, six periods. Use straight after the sheet it came from
purposes.structure/flow: input, three boxes, output. 16:9 only — in 9:16 use timeline or unit-ladder
purposes.structure/multiple-bridge: one multiple walked into another — trailing figure, what came out, forward figure, with the removal named on each connector. Three steps and two connectors, fixed. 16:9 only: there is no portrait bridge
purposes.structure/timeline: six dated events. For decisions or disclosures, never a financial series
purposes.structure/closing: three lines and a date. The last plate of a section
purposes.peers/peer-strip: one moment across several names — the move and the multiple. Not for comparing fundamentals
purposes.cycles/cycle-frame: the same metric at two moments, with the path between them. For arguing cyclicality
purposes.paper/headline-band-t1: the plain band. Default section title
purposes.paper/headline-band-t2: heavier treatment, for a section opener
purposes.paper/headline-band-t3: the loudest. Once per video — the thesis
purposes.shorts/hook-card-t1: ticker, move, hook, sub. The standard vertical opener
purposes.shorts/hook-card-t2: the same slots at a different weight, so cards do not all look alike
purposes.shorts/hook-card-t3: ticker, huge, hook, sub — one dominant number rather than a percentage
purposes.frames/media-frame-t1: a bordered area with caption and source. t1 is the lightest — for a busy image
purposes.frames/media-frame-t2: a bordered area with caption and source, middle weight
purposes.frames/media-frame-t3: a bordered area with caption and source, heaviest — for a sparse image
purposes.frames/capture-frame: for text captures: headline, body and a mark on what you are pointing at
purposes.room/wide: the establishing shot. Opens a section
purposes.room/wide-tight: the same set closer; the far wall stops being drawn. Use when a headline band needs the top third
purposes.room/desk-front: straight on at the desk. The workhorse for talking-to-camera
purposes.room/desk-corner: three-quarter on the desk. Has a caption slot for naming an object in the set
purposes.room/from-behind-the-monitor: over the screen backs toward him — he is reading, not addressing us
purposes.room/whiteboard-wall: for a structure plate; the wall gives the diagram a reason to be in the room
purposes.room/printer-corner: for paper — a filing, a transcript, a printout
purposes.room/doorway: arrival and exit. Pairs with host/walking-out-of-frame
purposes.room/wall-of-calls: the receipts wall — ticker, date and a one-word outcome per row
purposes.overlays/row-band: the row highlight. The only sanctioned way to emphasise a row
purposes.annotations/scrawl-oval-wide: the workhorse — circles a line of type or a headline
purposes.annotations/scrawl-oval-tight: one cell, one candle, one word
purposes.annotations/underline-swipe: two swipes under a line. Emphasis without enclosing
purposes.annotations/underline-tight: the same, for a cell or a single figure
purposes.annotations/strike-out: two crossing swipes. For a number that is wrong or stale
purposes.annotations/box-scrawl: a rough rectangle. For a block, not a line
purposes.annotations/bracket-rows: a tall bracket for grouping rows, with a note slot beside it
purposes.annotations/arrow-elbow: from a scrawled note to a target
purposes.annotations/caret-note: a caret with words above it, for an insertion
purposes.annotations/tick-marks: three ticks. For a list being confirmed

_note: One outfit per episode, the same in every frame of it — picked at ingest
or per workspace, never per shot. Every outfit keeps a mid-to-dark torso
and the darkest cloth at the trousers, so his separation from the room
survives whichever is chosen.

figure.how: an argument to the engine at ingest (--outfit)

medium.how: a different KEY, not an engine argument — the robe is drawn, not recoloured
